title: The circle of fifths
summary: All twelve keys in a ring, each a perfect 5th from the next.

steps.title: Circle of fifths
steps.body:
Start on C and go up a perfect 5th: G. Up another 5th: D. Then A, E, B. Each step adds one sharp. Go down in 5ths from C instead, to F, B♭, E♭, and each step adds one flat. Put all twelve keys in a ring this way and you have the **circle of fifths**.

**Why it matters:** It is a map of how keys relate. Keys next to each other share all but one note, which is why songs often move to a neighbouring key, and why the chords in Unit 5 follow the circle.

steps.title: Fifths down from C
steps.body: C, then down a 5th to F, then to B♭ and E♭: one more flat each time.

items.prompt: Play C4, then go up a perfect 5th to the next sharp key.
Play G4, then go down a perfect 4th. You land on D, the next key round the circle.
Going round the circle of fifths in the sharp direction, which key comes after G major?

steps.title: Walk the circle
steps.body: Play the tonic of each key round the circle: C G D A E B, each a 5th above the last. Then go the other way: C F B♭ E♭.

items.prompt: Going round the circle of fifths in the sharp direction, which key comes after A major?
Going round the circle of fifths in the flat direction, which key comes after F major?
Going round the circle of fifths in the flat direction, which key comes after C major?
